facts: The gradient of the secant through $P(c, f(c))$ and $Q(c+h, f(c+h))$ is the difference quotient $m_{\text{secant}}=\dfrac{f(c+h)-f(c)}{h}$, where $h\ne 0$.
As $h\to 0$, $Q$ approaches $P$ along the curve. When the difference quotient has a finite limit, that limit is the gradient of the tangent at $P$.
When this finite limit exists, working out the secant gradient for smaller and smaller $|h|$, such as $0.1$, $0.01$, $0.001$, estimates the tangent gradient at $x=c$.

The gap $h$ may be positive ($Q$ right of $P$) or negative ($Q$ left of $P$). For the tangent gradient to be given by a finite two-sided limit, the difference quotient must approach the same finite value from both sides.
